A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RRDA and retain matching methods, benchmarks, and principal results. All pages, equations, tables, and figures are readable, including the new appendices in v2; v1 ends with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original RRDA experiments on Office-31, Office-Home, and VisDA, together with optimization ablations, sensitivity studies, and feature visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and reports additional variance, initialization, runtime, and CLIP-integration results, including Tables 7–8 in the appendix.

M1.justification: The main entropy-based feature generation, extended classifier, and SHOT/AaD adaptation pipeline remain intact. Appendix B.2 adds a CLIP-specific adaptation using text-guided synthetic known features and optimized high-entropy unknown prototypes without fine-tuning the foundation model.

E1.justification: Evaluation remains on Office-31, Office-Home, and VisDA. The added CLIP and initialization experiments reuse existing datasets and classification tasks; no new dataset, domain, population, or openness scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their comparator sets. Appendix B.2/Table 8 introduces zero-shot CLIP as a comparator against CLIP+RRDA. The revised threshold comparison in Table 5 also drops the AaD-based row and reports only SHOT+RRDA.

E3.justification: Main benchmark splits, training budgets, and hyperparameters remain unchanged. Added protocols include frozen CLIP-ViT-B/32 with class-name prompts and a 0.5 log(25) unknown threshold, classifier-initialization controls, and A2D runtime measurements. Table 5 adds OS* and UNK reporting, but no longer specifies the A2D transfer task identified in v1.

E4.justification: The supporting analyses are substantially revised. v1's Office-31 comparison of unoptimized features, entropy-only optimization, and entropy-plus-diversity is replaced by an Office-Home variance-on/off ablation. The threshold analysis is replaced, and v2 adds classifier-initialization robustness and computational-overhead studies. The openness, K', convergence, and t-SNE analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability across runs. The variance regularizer concerns synthetic-feature diversity, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their results except for OSLPP's W2D entry, corrected from '9..6' to 93.6. Supporting results change substantially: the replacement variance ablation reports 64.7 versus 70.0 HOS, and Table 5 replaces the earlier SHOT/AaD scores with SHOT+RRDA HOS of 70.5–72.6 plus OS*/UNK results. New comparisons report initialization HOS of 93.2 versus 93.8, SHOT runtimes of 4m00s versus 4m31s with RRDA, and CLIP HOS of 57.6 versus 71.0 with RRDA. These are new or replaced results, not established same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the formal model composition from h composed with g to g composed with h, matching the stated encoder and classifier mappings. The unknown-feature selection criterion also explicitly applies softmax before entropy. The principal loss equations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: synthetic known/unknown features enable an extended classifier, allow closed-set source-free adaptation methods to handle open-set problems, and improve performance on three benchmarks. The CLIP experiment supplies additional support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 emphasizes the importance of variance regularization on difficult transfers and interprets the new initialization and runtime results as robustness and modest overhead. It replaces v1's threshold rationale and removes the warning that strict thresholds can exclude VisDA classes. Appendix C adds dependence on synthetic-feature quality and motivates adaptive selection of K'.

D1.justification: v1 specifies only noisy feature initialization; v2 identifies Gaussian noise drawn from N(0,1.0). The appendix documents the CLIP encoder, prompt template, detection threshold, and absence of fine-tuning, while Table 6 adds measured runtimes. Existing hardware, optimizer settings, training budgets, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bardes et al. (2022) to connect the variance regularizer with prior work, and cites Radford, Tang, Zara, and Singha for the foundation-model extension. The main related-work discussion and positioning against existing domain-adaptation approaches remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the introductory method summary, refines several method explanations and terms, introduces numbered section hierarchies, and organizes supplementary material into appendices. Most main-text prose and the overall narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a compact two-column layout to a single-column journal format. Figure 1 is redrawn with revised stage labels and an expanded legend; tables are resized and repositioned, Tables 4–5 are restructured, and Tables 6–8 are added. Figures 2–4 retain their underlying visual evidence.

improvement.justification: The new variance and initialization controls, runtime measurements, CLIP experiment, and explicit noise specification improve practical validation and reproducibility while preserving the main benchmark evidence. The gain is limited: v2 removes the original no-optimization control and replaces threshold results without a clearly matched transfer setting, weakening the traceability of that analysis.
